brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Something to keep sewing supplies tidy (organised storage for sewing notions and tools)
requirements.evidence: Three-cell caddy: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (full-depth, 3 compartments) for small notions, bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full (deep open bin) for bulkier items, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-half-div2 (shallow 2-compartment bin) for tools — all bolted as one body (lockJoints, capOpenFaces caps caps), with accessory:0#0,0#1 grab handle for carrying between table and shelf.

requirements.requirement: Staged so the sewing purpose is visible
requirements.evidence: No sewing-specific props exist in the catalogue (searched sewing/thread/yarn/fabric/needle/button/scissors), so it is dressed with generic equivalents: a tape measure, gaffer tape roll and electrical tape, tweezers, and a pencil cup (prop:9, which holds its own pencils) standing tall in the deep bin. Live check_build passes, meshClash clear, and all props are visible from above (look az 45/polar 30). Small heaps placed in the deep div3 compartments photographed below the rim, so that bin was left empty and clean rather than hiding props.

finish.summary: A 3-cell sewing-supplies caddy: a full-depth 3-compartment centre bin for pins, buttons and bobbins, a deep open bin for fabric/thread bulk (with a tall pencil cup for scissors, seam rippers and marking pencils), and a shallower 2-compartment bin for tools like the tape measure and tweezers. A grab handle on the centre cell makes the whole caddy portable; open faces are capped and joints locked. Check_build passes with meshClash clear. No sewing-specific props exist in the catalogue, so generic tape/tweezer/cup props stage its use.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
